Package frc.robot.subsystems.elevator

Class ElevatorConstants

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.subsystems.elevator.ElevatorConstants
public class ElevatorConstants extends Object
The physical description of one elevator, supplied to the IO that models or drives it.

These values come from CAD, from a team's own measurements, or from a previous robot. They are properties of a mechanism, not of the robot, which is why they are passed into the IO rather than being global constants the library owns: a team with two elevators constructs two of these, and a team reusing this library on a different robot writes its own values without editing the library. 


 ElevatorConstants constants = new ElevatorConstants()
     .withMotor(DCMotor.getKrakenX60(2))
     .withGearRatio(12.0)
     .withDrumRadius(Meters.of(0.0254))
     .withCarriageMass(Kilogram.of(8.0))
     .withTravel(Meters.of(0.0), Meters.of(1.0));

Why a mutable class with fluent setters. Java has no named arguments, so a twelve-parameter constructor would be unreadable and trivially mis-ordered. Every setter returns this and validates its input, which makes a mis-specified mechanism fail immediately at construction with a useful message instead of producing strange motion later.

Subclassing. A team that needs extra fields can extend this class. Consumers read through the accessors, so overridden values are honoured.

      public ElevatorConstants withCounterbalanceMass(edu.wpi.first.units.measure.Mass counterbalanceMass)

      public ElevatorConstants withSimulateGravity(boolean simulateGravity)
      Sets whether the simulation applies gravity.

      Turning gravity off makes the carriage hold any position trivially, which is useful when a test is about sequencing rather than control.

    • withGoalTolerance

      public ElevatorConstants withGoalTolerance(edu.wpi.first.units.measure.Distance goalTolerance)
      Sets the tolerance within which the carriage counts as at its target.

      Sized for a mechanism held by a software loop rather than a servo: a proportional loop settles with a small steady-state error against gravity, so an unrealistically tight tolerance would leave atGoal() false forever.

      Parameters:
      goalTolerance - the tolerance
      Returns:
      this, for chaining
